business_scope.primary_industry_name: Electron Beam 3D Melting of Porous Titanium Hip Joint Prosthetics

stage_1.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency / Certificate of Good Standing of the ultimate corporate shareholder
stage_1.issuing_entity: Companies registry in the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
stage_1.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961) by the competent issuing authority, or Consular Legalization where the issuer is not a Hague Convention party

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 (SARL), Article L.210-2 and R.123-1 et seq. (registration with RCS); Civil Code Article 1832.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS) through Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises, operated by INPI at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Formulaire M0 (Déclaration de création de société commerciale) – Cerfa n° 35768*01, accompanied by certified statutes
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: SARL has no legal minimum capital; one euro is sufficient. Cash contributions must be paid into a blocked escrow account at a French bank or held by a notary until provisional registration. Non-cash contributions require an independent value report (commissaire aux apports) if demanded by a shareholder or when the contribution exceeds €30,000 and exceeds half the share capital. For medical implant manufacturing, a subscribed capital of at least €100,000 is recommended to satisfy MDR compliance, product liability insurance, and cleanroom investment.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the capital of the company, as fixed in the draft statutes, be subscribed in full by the shareholders and paid in cash into a blocked escrow account at a credit institution in France, to be released after provisional registration. FURTHER RESOLVED: That the registered office be established at [registered address], France, as the company's permanent seat for administrative, tax, and regulatory purposes. FURTHER RESOLVED: That [Name] be appointed as Gérant, with full powers to represent the company, and [Name] as Regulatory Affairs Officer, responsible for ANSM filings, environmental compliance, and occupational safety. FINALLY RESOLVED: That the Gérant be authorised to complete RCS registration through the Guichet Unique and execute all documents required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Verification of company name availability and drafting of articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search existing French corporate names and trademark registrations to confirm the desired legal name is available. Draft French-language 'statuts' containing the corporate name, registered office, corporate purpose, share capital, shareholder contributions, SARL legal form, duration of 99 years, and appointment of initial management. Ensure the corporate purpose includes manufacture of titanium orthopedic implants and electron beam melting of porous surgical-grade titanium.
required_dossiers: Identity documents/passports of all shareholders
Draft statutes signed by all shareholders
Name availability search report from Infogreffe/INPI
Registered office address supporting document (lease, title deed, or free-use letter)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name conflicts with an existing trademark or corporate name, add a distinctive suffix or choose a new name and re-run the availability search; any trademark opposition should be resolved before submission to the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of legal incorporation notice in a legal announcement journal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Approved legal announcement journal (Journal d'Annonces Légales, JAL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and submit the 'avis de constitution' to a JAL approved by the local prefecture. Include the company name, legal form 'SARL', registered office address, share capital amount, corporate purpose, duration, and names of the Gérant managers. Obtain the official 'attestation de parution' bearing the journal title and date of publication.
required_dossiers: Text of the legal announcement
Registered office address
Proposed corporate name and legal form
Power of attorney if announcement is filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication notice is defective or omitted, publish a corrective notice ('rectificatif') in the same journal and request a renewed attestation; the error does not invalidate subsequent registration if cured before the RCS filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of paid-up capital in escrow
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French-licensed bank or notary (Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations eligible)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked account in the company's name and transfer all cash subscription amounts. Obtain a 'certificat de dépôt de fonds' from the bank or notary certifying receipt and blocking of the funds. If in-kind contributions exist, prepare the contribution list and appoint a 'commissaire aux apports' where required by law.
required_dossiers: Bank wire transfer receipts or SWIFT confirmations
Shareholder subscription list ('état de souscription du capital')
Capital deposit certificate issued by bank or notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to issue the certificate, complete enhanced KYC and source-of-funds documentation, then request re-issuance; if funds are rejected, re-transfer to an alternate French banking or notarial depositary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of formation dossier with Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online M0 declaration selecting SARL and the principal activity 'Manufacture of surgical and orthopedic instruments and titanium porous implants (APE/NAF 32.50A)'. Upload the statutory dossiers, sign electronically on behalf of all shareholders, select the competent RCS Greffe based on the registered office, and pay the applicable greffe fee.
required_dossiers: Formulaire M0 (Cerfa n° 35768*01)
Signed statutes
Attestation de parution in the legal announcement journal
Bank or notary capital deposit certificate
Proof of registered office and occupancy rights
Identity documents of legal representatives
Declaration of beneficial owner(s)
Power of attorney if filing through a mandatory
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Guichet Unique issues a query, respond within 15 calendar days through the online portal, upload missing documents or rectified information, and track the revised processing date; failure to respond results in rejection but the same dossier may be resubmitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration and issuance of K-bis extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Greffe verifies the legality of the statutes, the identity of shareholders and managers, the registered office, and the compatibility of the corporate purpose with the declared activity. Upon approval, the company is registered on the RCS, a SIREN/SIRET number is assigned, and the definitive 'extrait K-bis' is issued as the official certificate of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Complete formation application electronically transmitted by Guichet Unique
Receipt confirming approval from Guichet Unique
Any prior provisional RCS number or reference code
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe rejects the application, correct the precise legal grounds stated in the refusal, complete the missing legal formalities, and resubmit; a second refusal may be appealed under Article R.123-151 to the President of the Commercial Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notification of INSEE identifiers and finalisation of corporate records
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon RCS approval, submit the anti-money laundering and beneficial ownership declarations, obtain the definitive SIREN/SIRET and the VAT registration number (via Direction Générale des Finances Publiques), and open the corporate statutory records at the registered office including the share register, minutes of shareholders' and managers' decisions, and the beneficial owners register.
required_dossiers: K-bis extract
SIRET and APE code notification
VAT number notification
Corporate minute book and shareholder register opening form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the assigned SIRET or APE code is inaccurate, submit a rectification request via Guichet Unique under Article R.123-227-4 of the Code de commerce; incorrect VAT data will be corrected by the DGFiP by filing form P0.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: ANSM – Agence nationale de sécurité du médicament et des produits de santé, in coordination with a European Notified Body under EU Regulation 2017/745 (MDR); DREETS for workplace occupational inspection
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: EU MDR CE Certificate of Conformity and EUDAMED Manufacturer Registration; ICPE declaration / operating permit for the industrial facility

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: DREAL – Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (environmental authority)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: ICPE-Regime de Declaration for metal working and thermal treatment processes, subject to prior environmental screening (examen au cas par cas) where installed capacity or titanium powder storage exceeds minimum thresholds
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: pH 5.5–8.5, suspended solids ≤ 30 mg/L, COD ≤ 125 mg/L, titanium and vanadium concentration ≤ 0.5 mg/L each. Air emissions: metal particulates ≤ 10 mg/Nm³, VOCs ≤ 75 mgC/m³ in exhaust. Hazardous waste from titanium powder handling must be segregated, identified and sent to an authorised treatment facility under the waste nomenclature.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the prefectural Commission de Sécurité for handling of flammable metal powders; structural load certificate verifying floor resistance for electron-beam melting machines and cleanroom equipment; DREETS workplace inspection certifying compliance with Code du travail provisions on ionising/electron-beam shielding, machine guarding, personal protective equipment, and ventilation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via impots.gouv.fr portal
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities obtain SIREN/SIRET and TVA identification number through guichet-entreprises.fr or direct DGFiP registration formalities
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections available; limited to specific holding company regimes and hybrid mismatch adjustments under French tax code and EU directives

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time e-invoicing with API reporting and digital fiscal stamps for qualifying B2B transactions

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT rate on exports of goods outside the EU and qualifying offshore services upon proof of export
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Penalties up to 80% of evaded tax plus interest; potential criminal prosecution for fraudulent claims

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (national central bank within the Eurosystem of the European Central Bank) and the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) under the economic policy framework of the Ministry of Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a full member of the euro area, and the euro is freely convertible for both current and capital account transactions. There are no restrictive foreign exchange controls applicable to residents or non-residents. Profit remittances by a SARL to non-resident shareholders are permitted without prior authorisation, subject to withholding tax coordination under tax treaties, proof of corporate existence, and compliance with anti-money laundering (AML) and counter-terrorist financing (CTF) obligations. Capital account flows, including inbound equity injections and outbound dividends, are unrestricted. However, transaction-level statistical reporting to the Banque de France is mandatory for cross-border transfers exceeding €750,000 per transaction, and legal entities must report direct investment flows to the French Treasury for balance-of-payments and direct investment monitoring purposes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory timeline for export proceeds surrender and no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts in France. The euro being the domestic legal tender, exporters may invoice and receive settlement in foreign currency, hold the proceeds abroad, and convert at will. However, for commercial and statistical prudence, cross-border export receipts above €750,000 per transaction must be declared to the Banque de France via the standard reporting form for balance-of-payments purposes. French resident exporting entities must maintain full supporting documentation for a period of six years to satisfy customs and tax audit requirements. No obligation exists to channel export proceeds through a domestic French bank account.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BPCE Group (Natixis / Banque Populaire / Caisse d'Épargne)
CIC Banque Crédit Industriel et Commercial

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium for PSD2-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) incorporated in the EEA and passporting into France; Low for offshore or third-country digital EMIs operating outside the European Economic Area. Under the Second Payment Services Directive (PSD2), an EMI must be chartered in an EU member state and passported to France to offer cross-border payment and e-money services. Non-EEA fintech entities cannot open local bank accounts or provide payment services without obtaining a French licence from the ACPR (Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution). Even with ACPR licensing, the practical viability for clearing large trade disbursements is constrained by limits on holding client funds and the absence of fully-fledged credit services. For a medium-risk orthopedic implant manufacturer with Letters of Credit and SWIFT wiring needs, a tier-1 bank remains the legally safest and operationally robust clearing rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of directors is not an absolute statutory requirement in France, but French banks typically require personal appearance of at least one managing director or authorised signatory at account opening for foreign-controlled entities. Remote onboarding is permitted under ACPR guidance using certified video identity verification and electronic signatures, subject to robust KYC procedures, digital due diligence, and conformity with technical standards published by the CNIL (Commission nationale de l'informatique et des libertés) for biometric data. However, in practice, for a newly registered SARL with a non-resident shareholder, the responsible relationship manager will request one physical interview at the branch, or an electronic documentary authenticated via a trusted third party, to mitigate fake corporate identity risk. The KYC package must include the corporate legal opinion, certified copies of constitutional documents, proof of registered office, UBO declarations, and source-of-funds documentation for the capital deposit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder located in a high-risk jurisdiction or a jurisdiction with opaque beneficial ownership registers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Combined package containing notarised and apostilled statute of the SARL, a legal opinion from a qualified French attorney confirming valid incorporation and beneficial owner identification, individual identity documents of all UBOs, a source-of-wealth and source-of-funds narrative supported by tax returns, audited financial statements, bank reference letters from existing regulated institutions, and a detailed group structure diagram demonstrating legitimate commercial rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Industry mismatch or elevated risk profile for orthopedic implant manufacturing, including bilateral trade contracts with foreign hospitals or distributors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed master supply agreements, pro-forma invoices, certificates of product registration in France (CNEH/registration dossier), ISO 13485 certification for medical devices, MDR EU 2017/745 compliance certificates, major customer and supplier due-diligence files, and a credible business plan showing product flow, payment terms, and projected transaction volumes to establish commercial coherence and low AML risk.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection consisting of a large cross-border wire transfer from a third-country jurisdiction with non-transparent routing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sworn statement of lawful origin of funds, bank statement and SWIFT confirmation from the remitting bank showing the chain of accounts, authenticated translation of all corporate resolutions authorising the transfer, board approvals, and a legally certified copy of the corporate bank account at the sending institution, together with a notarised declaration by the beneficial owner confirming absence of sanctioned linkages or criminal activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexpected cash deposits or frequent transactions just below the statutory threshold for automatic declaration in the operational account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive ledger of commercial invoices with reference numbers, per-transaction contract or purchase order extracts, stock records, customs declarations (DAU), logistics documentation, and an internal AML-compliant transaction monitoring protocol documenting the reason for each transaction and the absence of structuring intent.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocols for inbound capital injection into the French SARL: execute a commercial-purpose SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for interbank cover) with a valid purpose code matching the capital account category, typically 'Investment in capital in a resident company' under the Banque de France balance-of-payments reporting classification. Accompanying verification must include the executed capital subscription agreement, notarised board minutes, representation of the new corporate shareholder (certified attestation), the bank's own UBO and negative-list screening confirmation, and prior declaration of direct investment to the French Treasury if the investor is from a non-EU jurisdiction or the investment surpasses statutory thresholds. All inbound transfers must clearly identify the originator and beneficiary exact legal name and account number. The receiving bank must be instructed to credit the funds to a dedicated 'Capital Escrow Account' or a newly opened operational account with a note 'apport en capital' to prevent commingling and facilitate seamless statutory publication of capital increase.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for outbound disbursements are executed via: (1) SWIFT MT103 for individual trade payments to suppliers and distributors with correct purpose codes (e.g., 'Prepayment of imports' or 'Payments for imports' under the French current account coding), including corresponding invoice and customs documents; (2) Documentary and Standby Letters of Credit (MT700, MT707) for structured purchase contracts, especially where the counterparty requires a bank undertaking before dispatch; and (3) MT202 COV for interbank wire cover where an MT103 knock-off is not possible. The SARL may use bank-executed commercial LC arrangements with the issuing French bank for inbound raw-material purchases and outbound finished-goods sales, provided the documentary bundle strictly conforms to the LC terms (invoice, bill of lading, packing list, certificate of origin). For tax and FX audit integrity, all outbound disbursements must be authorised by dual signatory protocols and must reference the applicable business relationship contract. For settlements involving non-EUR currencies, the bank automatically executes a spot or forward transaction under the umbrella treasury hedge agreement signed during the on-boarding phase.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) - permitted only in exceptional cases when the counterparty jurisdiction imposes capital controls; in France standard deliverable forwards are preferred
Vanilla FX Call and Put Options
Currency Swap with Commercial Reference Rate (CRR)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Shareholders’ Annual General Meeting – Approval of Annual Accounts (Assemblée Générale Ordinaire)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate body; minutes recorded in the corporate register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after each fiscal year end (e.g., by 30 June for a 31 December year-end).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene and hold the AGM allows any shareholder or the public prosecutor to apply to the court to order the meeting; the gérant may also face personal criminal liability for intentionally failing to prepare and submit annual accounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Filing with the Commercial Court Registry (Dépôt des comptes annuels au Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés – RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month of shareholder approval and no later than 7 months after fiscal year end (e.g., by 31 July for a 31 December year-end).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers an injunction and daily penalty (astreinte) ordered by the president of the commercial court; the company risks administrative strike-off (radiation) and court-imposed fines if the obligation remains unresolved.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return and Financial Statements Package (Liasse fiscale – Déclaration de résultats n° 2065)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques – Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 December year-end, due by the second business day after 1 May (generally 3 May); for a non-calendar fiscal year, due within 3 months of fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing interest of 0.20% per month plus a late assessment increase of 5% of the tax due, or 10% after formal notice; 40% penalty for bad faith and 80% for fraudulent conduct.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Declaration Update (Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs – mise à jour)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS Register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Not a standalone annual filing: update required within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership or in the information already filed.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or update the UBO declaration may suspend the legal entity’s ability to exercise voting rights and may result in administrative fines up to EUR 7,500 for natural persons and EUR 37,500 for legal persons.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Business Contribution Return (Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises – CFE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques – local tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual declaration submitted each year; payment due by 15 December for the current year (unless withdrawn by the tax authority).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A 10% late-payment increase and monthly interest of 0.20% are assessed on unpaid tax; persistent non-payment permits enforced collection from the company’s bank account or movable assets.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: For a French SARL, appointment of a statutory auditor (Commissaire aux Comptes) is mandatory when at least two of the following thresholds are exceeded at the balance sheet date: balance sheet total of EUR 4,000,000; net turnover of EUR 8,000,000; average headcount of 50 during the fiscal year. Mandatory audit also applies if the SARL controls or is controlled by another entity whose aggregate size meets the thresholds, or if shareholders representing at least one-third of the voting rights request a court-appointed audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Individual annual accounts must be prepared in accordance with French GAAP as set out in the ANC Regulation 2014-03 (Plan Comptable Général – PCG). IFRS is permitted for consolidated financial statements of groups satisfying certain EU transparency conditions, but not for the SARL’s individual statutory accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: French law does not impose a separate annual UBO confirmation filing. The beneficial owner declaration is lodged at incorporation and must be updated with the RCS within 30 days of any change. As a matter of annual governance best practice, the gérant and shareholders should verify the current UBO particulars at the AGM and, if needed, file an amended declaration with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce so that the register is accurate and enforceable.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Registre des procès-verbaux d’assemblées (Minutes and resolutions of general meetings)
Registre des mouvements de titres (Register of share transfers and ownership records)
Registre des décisions de l’associé unique (Register of sole shareholder decisions, if applicable)
Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs mis à jour (Beneficial ownership documentation and updated declaration)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 130 – USD 520 (EUR 120 – EUR 480) per year for professional registered-office domiciliation services in France
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 – USD 12,000 per year for a small to mid-sized SARL manufacturing orthopedic implants, depending on entity size, complexity of transactions, and audit firm standing.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25.000% standard rate under CGI Art. 219 (fiscal years opening on or after 1 January 2022); top effective rate 25.825% inclusive of the 3.3% social contribution surcharge levied on CIT exceeding EUR 763,000 for companies with turnover above EUR 7,630,000.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% reduced rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for SMEs satisfying CGI Art. 219 I-b conditions (turnover below EUR 10,000,000, fully paid share capital, 75% individual ownership). R&D tax credit (Crédit d'Impôt Recherche) at 30% of eligible R&D expenditure up to EUR 100,000,000 and 5% above that cap, credited against CIT and refundable over 3 years; Innovation tax credit (Crédit d'Impôt Innovation) at 30% of eligible prototype/design costs up to EUR 400,000 for SMEs; Young Innovative Company (JEI) regime available if qualifying R&D represents at least 15% of tax-deductible expenses, conferring CIT exemption (37.5% up to yearly cap), payroll-tax relief, and exemption from the 3.3% social surcharge.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carryforward with no statutory expiry; annual utilization is capped at EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of the taxable profit exceeding EUR 1,000,000 (CGI Art. 209). One-year carryback of up to EUR 1,000,000 under CGI Art. 220 quinquies, converted into a refundable tax credit (créance d'impôt) repayable in five annual instalments.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Cerfa n° 2065-SD (annual corporate income tax return) together with the 2050-series 'liasse fiscale' schedules (2052-SD to 2059-SD) and tax-credit schedule n° 2072-CI-SD. Mandatory electronic filing on the impots.gouv.fr professional portal in EDI (Échange de Données Informatisé) or EFI (Échange de Formulaire Informatisé) mode. The return is filed once annually; interim CIT is discharged through four quarterly advance payments (acomptes) and one final balance (solde).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with quarterly advance payments due 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December of each fiscal year, and the final balance paid with the annual return).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending 31 December, the return must be filed by the second working day following 1 May (ordinarily 3 May). For a fiscal year not aligned with the calendar year, the deadline is the second working day following the expiry of three months and fifteen days after the fiscal year-end. The final CIT balance is payable on the filing deadline; advance payments follow the quarterly schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification: SIREN number, RCS registration, APE/NAF code, registered-office address, share capital, and tax regime election (Article 206 or 239 bis AA option).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SARL files under its French SIREN; non-resident managers must appoint a tax domiciliary (représentant fiscal) if the company has no permanent establishment of substance in France, and the representative's details must be entered.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Election of taxable regime: corporate income tax (Impôt sur les Sociétés) at 25% standard rate; start-up option for pass-through taxation available for the first five fiscal years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: An SARL is subject to CIT by default; the election for transparent taxation is declared on the first return and binds for five years; non-resident shareholders are then taxed on their profit share directly.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: 2065-SD, Box QF (Bénéfice taxable au taux réduit)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit eligible for the 15% reduced rate within the EUR 42,500 band for qualifying SMEs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm SME eligibility annually: turnover below EUR 10,000,000, fully-paid capital, and 75% direct or indirect individual ownership throughout the fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income (résultat fiscal) disclosed on the balance-sheet schedule and carried to the headline boxes XA/XB of form 2065-SD, after statutory add-backs (réintégrations) and deductibility adjustments (extractions).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductibility of group royalties, interest, management fees and intercompany charges must be justified by a transfer-pricing analysis under CGI Art. 57; non-substantiated charges are re-integrated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Imputation of prior-year losses against current-year taxable profit and the remaining loss carryforward balance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The annual cap EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of profit above EUR 1,000,000 applies; document the loss trail in the 2058-B-SD schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT liability computed at 25% on the portion of profit not covered by the 15% band, with credits (CIR, CII) imputed and the solde payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Refundable credits available to unprofitable years are repaid by the tax administration; any offset against withholding taxes due on shareholder distributions is separately reconciled.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The 3.3% social contribution surcharge applies to the CIT exceeding EUR 763,000 for companies with turnover of at least EUR 7,630,000.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The surcharge applies regardless of shareholder residence; no treaty relief is available for this national surcharge.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual schedule of tax credits and, for large enterprises, the transfer-pricing declaration (Art. 223 quinquies B).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Form 2257 is obligatory when consolidated group turnover or balance-sheet total exceeds EUR 400,000,000 and lists related-party flows; below the threshold, the SARL must still retain documentary justification for each cross-border controlled transaction.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or non-filing triggers a 10% penalty (majoration) on CIT due; where a formal notice is ignored, the penalty rises to 40%, and to 80% where concealment is intentional (CGI Art. 1728); late-payment interest (intérêt de retard) accrues at 0.20% per month (2.4% annualized) for the entire period of delay; a 5% penalty applies for failure to pay tax after notice (CGI Art. 1731). False declarations attract 40% penalty plus interest; fraud (CGI Art. 1741) carries criminal exposure of up to five years' imprisonment and EUR 500,000 fine (7 years and EUR 3,000,000 for aggravated cross-border fraud).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% domestic withholding tax on distributions paid by a French company to non-resident corporate shareholders (CGI Art. 119 bis 2), where the distribution exceeds the share-capital basis exemption; distributions to non-resident individuals are subject to the 12.8% flat tax (prélèvement forfaitaire unique) plus, for French-resident recipients, social levies. The French payer files form n° 2756 on the SEPA date of the distribution and pays the withholding to the Direction Générale des Finances Publiques.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke the France-China DTA (1984 treaty, amended by 2013 Protocol), the non-resident parent must (i) submit a valid Chinese Tax Resident Certificate (TRC) covering the distribution date to the French paying company before payment is made, (ii) certify beneficial ownership of the dividends and absence of an artificial arrangement designed to obtain treaty benefits under the Principal Purpose Test (MLI and L.64 LPF abuse-of-law doctrine), and (iii) hold the qualifying shareholding; the treaty rate is 10% for companies holding directly at least 25% of the SARL's capital and 15% in other cases, with full exemption available under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (CGI Art. 119 ter) where the parent EU company holds at least 10% of capital with no minimum holding period required. Where relief has been applied but the conditions are not met, the French administration collects the differential and penalties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: domestic withholding under CGI Art. 182 B applies at 25% for fiscal years opened on or after 1 January 2021 on payments for patents, trademarks, know-how, and technical assistance made by a French SARL to non-resident beneficial owners; the France-China DTA caps royalty withholding at 10% (and at 6% for royalties derived from cinematographic films and certain equipment rentals under the treaty's specific provisions), conditioned on TRC and beneficial-ownership proof. Interest: French domestic law imposes no withholding on arm's-length interest paid to non-resident corporate lenders established in cooperative jurisdictions, except a 75% levy on payments to persons domiciled in non-cooperative States (CGI Art. 125 A III); the France-China DTA reduces permissible withholding on interest to 10% as a protective cap, and the parent-subsidiary current account interest is deductible only if the thin-capitalization and related-party conditions of CGI Arts. 212 and 39 are observed.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400,000,000 (consolidated group turnover or balance-sheet total) triggers the mandatory Master File, French Local File, and annual transfer-pricing declaration (form n° 2257-SD) under CGI Art. 223 quinquies B. Below this threshold, the SARL is not exempt from demonstrating arm's-length pricing on demand: it must retain contemporaneous comparability analysis, intercompany agreements, budgets, and pricing formulas for each controlled transaction, and the absence of documentation will shift the burden of proof to the taxpayer upon audit.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not administer a formal Economic Substance Regulations filing (UAE-style ESR), but the substance-over-form doctrine, the abuse-of-law regime (LPF Art. L.64), the anti-artificial-arrangement doctrine (CGI Art. 155 A for services, Art. 57 for transfer pricing), and the BEPS anti-abuse rules (ATAD interest limitation, CFC rules under CGI Art. 209 B for profits routed through low-tax subsidiaries) require the SARL to demonstrate real local substance: a registered office, operational premises, employees performing engineering and manufacturing functions, board meetings held in France, and a commercial rationale for the central functions (R&D, quality certification of titanium orthopedic implants, sterilization, logistics). A letterbox SARL with management and decision-making abroad triggers recharacterization, recomputation of French taxable income, 40%-80% penalties, and denial of treaty benefits under the Principal Purpose Test.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate concealment of taxable profit through fictitious invoicing, undisclosed offshore bank accounts, computer data destruction, or accounting forgery; using a non-cooperative jurisdiction to shelter revenue from the 3D-printing implant manufacturing and sales; artificially booking export commissions to related distributors without services rendered.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Five years' imprisonment and EUR 500,000 fine under CGI Art. 1741; aggravated cross-border or organized fraud attracts seven years' imprisonment and EUR 3,000,000 fine, together with confiscation of assets, publication of the decision, and a ten-year professional ban.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant is jointly and severally liable under LPF Art. L.267 for tax, interest, and penalties where the fraudulent management caused the corporate tax debt; criminal courts may order restitution, asset freezing, travel bans (interdiction de quitter le territoire), and imprisonment of the gérant for intentional participation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file the 2065-SD liasse within the statutory deadline, filing an incomplete liasse, or dissimulating taxable profit through under-invoicing of implant sales to foreign related importers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: 10% penalty for late filing, 40% when filed after formal notice, 80% for intentional concealment plus 0.2% monthly late-payment interest (CGI Art. 1728); hidden income is recharacterized with a 40% penalty under Art. 1729 for bad faith and 80% for manoeuvres frauduleuses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who engineered the concealment face personal liability for the company's tax arrears (LPF Art. L.267), disqualification from commercial management, and criminal sanctions for falsified accounting records.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Misstatement and Thin Capitalization
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting implant sale prices, titanium powder procurement fees, royalty flows, or management charges at non-arm's-length levels; shifting profits to a non-resident related purchaser; excessive interest on shareholder loans exceeding the thin-capitalization ratio (debt-to-equity 1.5:1) or EBITDA limitation (25% of EBITDA with EUR 5,000,000 floor and 150% equity test).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment by the DGFiP under CGI Art. 57 with add-back of the non-deductible excess; 40% penalty for lack of bona fide pricing evidence, 80% for artificiality; interest at 0.2% monthly; applicability of the exchange-of-information and MAP procedures where double taxation arises.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant who signed the intercompany agreements and the CIT return may be personally assessed for the reassessed tax where the pricing arrangement was designed to evade French tax; criminal exposure under Art. 1741 if documents were falsified.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Artificial Arrangement and Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a letterbox SARL with no genuine manufacturing, staffing, or decision-making substance solely to access France's treaty network, the EU Parent-Subsidiary exemption, or the 15% reduced rate; structuring dividend flows through a conduit entity lacking economic activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits under the Principal Purpose Test (MLI); recharacterization under LPF Art. L.64 abus de droit with an 80% penalty on the tax benefit; refusal of the reduced rate and reinstatement of 25% withholding plus interest; possible joint liability of the parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face corrective reassessment personally for abus de droit when they personally engineered the artificial chain; in fraudulent schemes, imprisonment and fines under Art. 1741, and interdiction de gérer (management ban) for up to fifteen years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Beneficial Ownership and Payment Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to register the beneficial owners of the SARL in the Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE); receiving third-party payments, nominee-controlled Swift wire transfers, or concealable cash payments for implant shipments; violating the EUR 1,000 consumer cash-payment cap or using unknown intermediary bank accounts contrary to TRACFIN declaration obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Failure to file the RBE declaration: six months' imprisonment and EUR 15,000 fine for the gérant, EUR 75,000 for the company (Monetary and Financial Code Arts. L.561-2 ff., L.562-5 ff.); AML administrative sanctions up to EUR 5,000,000 or 10% of turnover by the ACPR; banking penalties on the prohibited payment rails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant is personally liable for RBE omissions; money-laundering complicity involving commercial funds attracts ten years' imprisonment and EUR 750,000 fine (Penal Code Art. 324-1 ff.), confiscation of the titanium implant inventory and proceeds, and travel restrictions.
